newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU offers judgment on EMU impact of certain bonds.
newsitem.headline: EU offers judgment on EMU impact of certain bonds.

text.p: The European Union announced on Wednesday several decisions which affect the budgetary treatment of deep-discounted and index-linked government bonds ahead of economic and monetary union.
In an effort to clarify the circumstances under which such bonds would have an impact on government deficits in 1997, Eurostat, the EU's statistical office said the following:

"For short-term bonds, the difference between the issue price and the nominal value is to be regarded as interest recorded at the issuance of the bonds; this difference has therefore an impact on the government deficit.

For medium and long-term bonds, however, Eurostat said the difference between the issue price and the nominal value of a government bond should not be recorded as interest and therefore has no impact on a government's deficit.

Regarding deep-discounted bonds -- those whose nominal coupon is less than 50 percent of the corresponding yield to maturity -- the office said the difference between the issue price and nominal value should be regarded as interest.
As a result, there is a corresponding impact on the deficit.
Eurostat noted that deep-discounted bonds are rarely used among EU governments.
Lastly, two distinct treatments were announced in the case of index-linked bonds.
For example, where the bond is linked to a consumer price index, the so-called "capital uplift" due to the movement of the index should be treated as interest and recorded when the bond is redeemed.
Eurostat said such treatment was in line with that used by Britain.

Alternatively, if the bond is linked to a financial asset, such as a foreign currency or gold, the capital uplift should be treated as a capital gain or loss. The ruling noted this was in line with the approach used by the Greek government.
